chapters.title: From idea to first sketch
chapters.text: I mapped out a first-person path with stops on either side and a destination that feels close even when there’s a long way to go.

chapters.title: Putting the camera on the road
chapters.text: I started with simple Blender geometry to check distance, scale and framing. Then I revised the road and islands, alternated the viewpoints and added a slight camera bank on turns.

chapters.title: From blockout to photorealism
chapters.text: Real photographs guided the shapes of Amandola, Camerino, London and Politecnico. I kept the Blender framing as a guide while developing the stone, sunlight from the left and orange mist.

chapters.title: Making the frames agree
chapters.text: I refined ten keyframes in reverse order, starting with the final temple. That kept the temple, path and buildings recognizable even in the most distant views.

chapters.title: One completed generation
chapters.text: I gave Seedance 2.5 Video Edit the Blender camera guide and all ten approved frames together. After a provider error with Kling, the first completed generation joined every stop in one take without regenerating individual clips.

sketchAlt: Original sketch of a path passing two islands and ending at a temple.
